FunMel

From fungal confrontation photographs to matched-control results.

FunMel measures the colour, shape and image-darkness profiles of approximately round Zymoseptoria tritici colonies around another fungus. It separates target colonies from central fungal tissue and connected hyphal growth, retains image provenance, and compares each treatment with controls from its own experimental set.

Get started · Real 14-day tutorial · All function examples

Melanization index is MI = 100 - CIELAB L*. Higher MI means darker pixels; it is not a direct measurement of melanin concentration. Lighting, calibration and image masks affect the result. Central hyphal growth is not an inhibition zone.

Install 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel")

Restart R before loading an updated package, then run:

library(FunMel)
packageVersion("FunMel")

R >= 4.1 and source-compilation tools are required: Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, matching Rtools on Windows, or R development tools and ImageMagick development libraries on Linux. To install local tutorials:

remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel",build_vignettes=TRUE,dependencies=TRUE)
vignette("FunMel",package="FunMel")
vignette("Real-14-day",package="FunMel")

Choose your starting point

Your task Start here
Learn with supplied photographs Follow the separate real 14-day tutorial
Analyze new photographs Prepare once, run, then finish as shown below
Revisit saved work Load the existing project; do not prepare it again
Explore specialist tools Use the complete function catalog

Review assignments before measurement and inspect QC before interpretation. Valid runs proceed automatically. Missing labels, unmatched controls, invalid settings and failed photographs still require correction.

New photographs: prepare, run, finish

1. Prepare once 

project <- prepare_experiment()
# Select a photo ZIP or one ORIGINAL photo inside the intended photo folder.

A file chooser selects files, not folders. Selecting one photograph uses its containing folder and subfolders, including all supported photographs there. The package prints that folder explicitly. For several batches, supply their common root folder or select a ZIP containing all batches and their controls:

# Alternative to the chooser; replace this example path.
project <- prepare_experiment("/full/path/to/photos","FunMel_project")

Use a new output folder for a new project. Existing nonempty folders are protected. A selected project/analysis RDS reopens its existing project instead of being treated as photographs. A metadata CSV, QC PDF or SVG is not a photo input.

A unique plate_metadata.csv in the input is read automatically; otherwise a template is created. Explicit folders such as batch1/control/ and batch1/fungus_A/ propose matching groups, but cannot prove biological identity. For nested ZIPs, relative paths distinguish repeated basenames. Supply one combined metadata table through metadata= when needed.

project$metadata_file
metadata <- read.csv(project$metadata_file,check.names=FALSE)
metadata[,c("plate_id","set_id","treatment","centre_model")]
validate_metadata(metadata)

Check the metadata against laboratory records and correct missing or inaccurate assignments before measuring.

Field Meaning
file, relative_file, plate_id Image provenance and globally unique independent plate identity
set_id Treatment plates and their own relevant controls
treatment Exact control label or the actual treatment name
centre_model, partner_type Normally none for controls and fungus for confrontation plates
day, medium, zymo_strain Complete and constant within a set once recorded; entirely unrecorded fields may stay blank
Other columns Preserved experimental annotations, including custom columns

One control plus three treatment plates means four metadata rows sharing a set. Enter the control once. Four target colonies and multiple spots within a plate are subsamples, not independent biological replicates. Repeated photographs of one plate are repeated observations, not extra independent plates.

2. Measure and inspect 

dish_mm <- 90 # Replace with the verified outer dish diameter (mm).
result <- run_experiment(project,dish_diameter_mm=dish_mm,max_dim=1200,
                         n_spots=5,spot_radius_mm=0.4)
result$analysis_status
result$failed
project$qc_dir

Successful processing reports "complete" and zero failed images. Inspect every QC PNG: target masks, central fungus/hyphae, spot positions, scale, illumination, shadows and warnings. Genuine failures must be corrected before finalization.

Omit spot settings for whole-colony measurements alone. Spots are additional, non-overlapping regions placed by a deterministic spatial-spread algorithm. Inspect n_spots_measured and spot_status; incomplete summaries are unavailable. Keep scale and sampling settings consistent across compared plates.

3. Finish and plot 

reviewed <- finish_experiment(project)
reviewed$melanization_coefficient
reviewed$assessment$status
print(plot_treatment_comparison(project))

Finalization reads saved measurements and current valid metadata, then exports tables, an assessment RDS and a comparison figure in PDF, SVG and 600-dpi PNG. Different recorded day/strain/medium contexts are finalized separately; context_index.csv identifies those folders.

Saved work: reopen without remeasuring 

project <- load_experiment() # Choose project.rds in its current folder.
result <- read_experiment(project)
head(result$spots)
reviewed <- read_experiment(project,finalized=TRUE) # If already finalized.
print(plot_treatment_comparison(project))
# Recompute final tables after valid annotation corrections when needed:
reviewed <- finish_experiment(project)

Final outputs saved means finalization succeeded. Do not prepare another project simply to display its existing results. Keep the complete project folder together; loading reconnects moved internal paths. External photo locations remain external. Saved results can be read and finalized without original photographs; remeasurement still requires them. Missing metadata is never guessed. project$result_file is a filename; result$spots is a measurement table.

Understand the measurements and statistics

A plate’s MI is the equally weighted mean of its target-colony MI_mean values. The coefficient is mean(treatment plate MI) / mean(own-set control plate MI). Controls are never pooled across matching sets. Values above 1 indicate darker image-based treatment means, not fold changes in pigment concentration.

MI_min/mean/max describe eligible whole-colony pixels. spots.csv stores each ROI’s pixel summaries; MI_spot_mean/min/max summarize individual spot means. These are different responses, not confidence limits. Default coefficients use whole-colony MI; a prespecified spot-based descriptive response can use melanization_coefficient(reviewed,response="MI_spot_mean").

Independent plates are biological units. One control per set permits descriptive ratios but yields assessment$status="insufficient_plate_replication"; that is an expected design limitation, not a software failure. With adequate replication, assessment uses lme4/lmerTest, matched contrasts and Holm adjustment. Review design, assumptions, model diagnostics and confounding before interpreting inference. The comparison plot itself is descriptive: bars show between-plate SD, not confidence intervals; ratio SD omits shared-control uncertainty.

Illumination correction may be withheld when fitted gains saturate. Inspect flat_field_status and warnings in plates.csv. Withholding does not establish adequate lighting, and ratios do not guarantee cancellation of exposure bias.

Custom metadata names and values remain in the full metadata and metadata_used.csv; measurement-name conflicts receive a metadata_ prefix only in measurement tables. Changed segmentation layouts require reanalysis.

Real data and every exported function

The real-data tutorial uses eight photographs from two sets, each with one control and three treatment plates. It includes the full file mapping, metadata, five spots per colony, QC examples, table definitions, coefficient calculations, final plots, exports and reopening instructions. The illustrative 90-mm scale requires physical verification for scientific use. Review image masks and calibration before using measurements in a study.

# Complete, noninteractive practice script in a new temporary project folder:
source(system.file("examples","walkthrough_14_days.R",package="FunMel"))
# All 42 exported functions, including specialist utilities:
source(system.file("examples","06_all_functions.R",package="FunMel"))

Interactive annotation is clearly marked and needs user clicks. The synthetic classifier example demonstrates the API; validate a classifier against annotated photographs before using it for a study. The algorithm overview explains the algorithms and how FunMel can complement ImageJ/Fiji.

Comparison captions are exported separately as treatment_comparison_caption.txt. Use caption="brief" or caption="full" in plot_treatment_comparison() to include a caption beneath the figure.
